title: Distribution-Connected Data Centers: Integration into Grid and DER Management Systems
content: Distribution-connected data centers introduce concentrated electricity demand that can strain feeders and substations. On the other hand, they hold a potential to provide operational flexibility by adjusting selected computing workloads and cooling demand or by using on-site energy resources. This article presents the author’s perspective, informed by a focused literature review, on integrating distribution-connected data centers into Advanced Distribution Management Systems (ADMS) and Distributed Energy Resource Management Systems (DERMS). The author proposes a simplified representation that separates IT, cooling, and auxiliary demand and examines how utilities can use it to assess network constraints and qualify facility flexibility for dispatch. Two integration architectures are considered, one based on coordination through a dedicated facility energy management system and the other on telemetry and authorized supervisory control through utility SCADA. The discussion examines the operational challenges these facilities create for distribution utilities and the potential benefits of using their flexibility. The article concludes by identifying operational priorities and open research questions.
